title: Platform systems & services: how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospectives, and roadmap (Q4 2025)
author: Elena Rodriguez
summary: Consolidated reference for platform systems & services: operational how-tos, dashboard catalogue, alert definitions, runbooks for common incidents, recent retrospectives, and the Q4 2025 roadmap. Intended as the canonical team wiki entry for oncall and platform engineering.
body:
Overview:

This document centralizes operational guidance for Redwood Inference platform systems and services. It includes: an inventory of critical services, step-by-step how-tos for common platform tasks, the canonical dashboard and alert catalogue, runbooks for prioritized incidents, a summary of recent retrospectives with action items, and the platform roadmap for Q4 2025 - Q1 2026.

Audience: platform engineers, SREs, oncall, infra, and service owners.

--

1) Systems & services inventory (short):

- platform-api: public REST edge for account, routing, and telemetry ingestion. Owner: platform-api team. SLO: 99.95% availability, p95 latency < 120ms for authenticated requests.
- inference-runtime: GPU-backed model serving mesh (batcher + runtime nodes + KV cache). Owner: serving-runtime. SLO: 99.9% availability for Dedicated tier, p95 generation latency depends on model but baseline p95 < 500ms for small models.
- routing-service: policy-based request router (cost/latency/region). Owner: routing. SLO: 99.95% availability.
- metrics-collector (telemetry-ingest): aggregates Prometheus metrics and traces, writes to TSDB. Owner: observability. Retention: 30d high-res, 365d aggregated.
- batcher: request batching service used by inference-runtime to increase throughput. Owner: serving-runtime. Scaling: HPA based on queue length and GPU occupancy.
- kv-cache: prefix and KV cache service (Redis cluster + persistence). Owner: serving-runtime. RTO: 15m for single-shard failover.
- edge-proxy: TLS termination and web WAF (ingress). Owner: infra-networking.
- cost-aggregator: nightly job that maps token usage to cost buckets. Owner: finance-infra.

Each service page should link to its detailed runbook (see related_pages).

2) How-tos (quick reference):

A. Add a Grafana dashboard panel to the Platform Overview dashboard:
1. Open Grafana -> Dashboards -> Platform Overview.
2. Click "Edit" -> "Add panel".
3. Use PromQL: sum(rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{service="platform-api"}[1m])) by (route) to show requests/s by route.
4. Set panel refresh 10s, panel owner as platform-oncall.
5. Commit dashboard change and add to PR for review (see dashboard PR template).

B. Emergency scale of inference-runtime GPU pool (when latency or queue growth is sustained > 5m):
1. Notify oncall and post summary in #platform-oncall (include cluster, region, job-id).
2. Check batcher queue length: kubectl -n serving-runtime get deployment batcher -o yaml and kubectl top pods -n serving-runtime --selector=app=batcher.
3. If queue depth > 10k and GPU utilization < 85%: increase node-pool GKE autoscaling target or bump dedicated pool size: gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize <group> --size=<new-size>. For Private installs, follow customer onprem runbook.
4. If GPUs are saturated: temporarily enable burst routing to Hosted fallback model-variant (routing-service: POST /v1/policies/override) or raise capacity on Dedicated pool.
5. After stabilization, document change in the incident channel and run the postmortem checklist.

C. Rotate TLS cert on edge-proxy (non-prod):
1. Create new cert via internal-CA: vault write pki/issue/platform-edge common_name=platform.example.com ttl=720h.
2. Upload cert to secret manager and trigger rolling restart: kubectl rollout restart deployment edge-proxy -n infra-networking.
3. Verify in Grafana: TLS cert expiry panel shows new expiry.

3) Dashboards & alert catalogue (canonical):

A. Platform Overview (Grafana): Owner: observability; Panels: total requests/s, error rate (5m), p50/p95/p99 latency by service, 1h cost per token estimate, GPU utilization top-10 nodes, queue depth (batcher).

B. Model Serving Latency (Grafana): Owner: serving-runtime; Panels: p50/p90/p95/p99 generation latency, KV cache hit ratio, model cold-start count, tokens/s by model family.

C. Cost & Billing (Grafana): Owner: finance-infra; Panels: daily cost, cost-per-token, predicted month-end spend, reserved capacity utilization.

D. Alerts (Frequent, with rationale):
- alert_platform_api_high_error_rate: triggers when 5m error rate > 2% and requests/s > 10. Severity: P1 (PagerDuty). Notify: #platform-oncall. Runbook: platform-api runbook.
- alert_inference_runtime_p95_latency: triggers when p95 generation latency > 800ms for 5m. Severity: P1. Actions: check batcher queue, scale GPU pool, enable fallback routing.
- alert_batcher_queue_growth: triggers when queue length increases > 200% over 10m. Severity: P1. Actions: validate worker availability, check redis latency, scale batcher.
- alert_gpu_node_disk_pressure: node reports disk_pressure=true. Severity: P2. Actions: cordon node, migrate pods, raise infra ticket.
- alert_metrics_collector_backfill_lag: when Prometheus remote write lag > 15m. Severity: P2. Actions: restart collector, check network congestion.

Alert routing: PagerDuty -> primary oncall -> escalation to platform-eng lead after 15m. Post initial page, always post summary to #platform-incidents with links to runbook and dashboard.

4) Canonical runbooks (examples):

Runbook: inference-runtime p95 latency (file reference: related runbook page) - Symptoms:
- Customers report slow responses or SLOs breached: p95 > 800ms.
- Grafana: Model Serving Latency dashboard shows spike.

Steps (ordered):
1. Triage: Confirm alert context (duration, models affected, region).
2. Live diagnostics: Login to cluster (gcloud container clusters get-credentials) and run: kubectl -n serving-runtime top pods --sort-by=cpu.
3. Check batcher queue length: redis-cli -h redis-serving TTL/llen for primary queue; or check queue metric in Grafana.
4. If queue length growing and GPUs underutilized: increase batcher replicas: kubectl scale deploy/batcher --replicas=<current+2> -n serving-runtime.
5. If GPUs saturated: increase GPU pool via cloud provider or enable routing fallback to hosted small-model variant (routing-service).
6. If KV cache miss rate spiked: verify redis cluster health: redis-cli INFO and check I/O wait; if node down, failover per kv-cache failover procedure.
7. If pod OOMs or repeated restarts: capture logs (kubectl logs -p), increase pod memory limit temporary, and redeploy.
8. Communicate: update incident channel with findings and mitigation steps.
9. Post-incident: open retro doc linking metrics and root cause, propose action items (see retrospectives).

Runbook: platform-api 5xx spike - Symptoms:
- Increased 5xxs, customers seeing errors for endpoints.

Steps:
1. Validate: Grafana -> Platform Overview -> 5xx panel, note affected endpoints.
2. Check recent deploys: gitlab CI pipeline, matching commit/rollout. If related, roll back: kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-api -n platform-api --to-revision=<previous>.
3. Inspect logs (kubectl logs --since=15m -l app=platform-api) and trace sampling in Tempo.
4. If DB errors: check connection pool saturation (rds performance insights) and restart workers or increase DB connections.
5. If downstream outage (e.g., identity service): open incident with downstream owner and apply temporary rate-limiting.
6. Inform oncall and affected stakeholders; start postmortem if severity P1.

5) Recent retrospectives (summary & action items):

Retrospective: High latency incident (2025-10-22) - Finding: autoscaling thresholds for GPU pools were conservative; cold-starts contributed to p99 spikes for large models. - Actions:
- Adjust autoscaler policy: lower threshold to 65% GPU util instead of 75% (action owner: infra-capacity; due: 2025-11-05).
- Implement warm-pool for popular models (action owner: serving-runtime; due: 2025-12-01).
- Add synthetic load tests to CI that simulate mixed small+large model workload; run nightly.

Retrospective: Dashboard alert fatigue (2025-09-14) - Finding: multiple low-signal alerts created noise.
- Actions:
- Consolidate related error-rate alerts into a composite alert (owner: observability; done: 2025-10-01).
- Adopt alert runbook template and severity rubric (owner: SRE; due: 2025-11-15).

6) Platform roadmap (Q4 2025 -> Q1 2026 highlights):

- Q4 2025:
  - Decrease model cold-start rate by implementing warm pools for top-20 models. Owner: serving-runtime. Target: reduce median cold-start latency by 30%.
  - Observability: migrate high-cardinality traces to sampled storage, add per-tenant cost dashboards. Owner: observability.
  - Dedicated capacity improvements: expose finer-grained autoscaling knobs and burst credits. Owner: dedicated-capacity.

- Q1 2026:
  - Private deployment packaging: automated air-gapped installer and KMS/HSM integration. Owner: private-deployments.
  - Runtime kernel selection improvements: per-model kernel heuristics to reduce p95 by 10%. Owner: serving-runtime-research.

Roadmap notes: each roadmap item must have a strategy doc and acceptance criteria in product docs before development. Use feature flag + canary for rollouts.

7) Team wiki & ownership (process):

- All service owners must keep a one-page service descriptor (ownership, SLOs, escalation contacts, runbook link) in the team wiki.
- Oncall rotations: primary (1 week) + secondary (week) + Platform Eng lead (monthly) escalation. Rota managed in PagerDuty.
- Postmortem policy: P1 incidents require a postmortem within 72h and an action-item owner assigned.

8) Templates and artifacts (links & examples):

- Runbook template: include symptoms, metrics to check, ordered mitigation steps, communication checklist, post-incident tasks.
- Dashboard PR template: title, panel description, PromQL/ELK query, owner, test plan, reviewers.
- Postmortem checklist: timeline, impact (customers, SLO), root cause, mitigations, action items with owners and due dates.

9) Appendices: commands, snippets, and contact list

- Useful commands:
  - kubectl -n serving-runtime get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference-runtime
  - kubectl logs deploy/batcher -n serving-runtime --tail=500
  - redis-cli -h redis-serving INFO
  - gcloud container clusters get-credentials <cluster> --zone <zone> --project <proj>

- Example alert snippet (Prometheus-rule):
  ALERT inference_runtime_p95_latency
  IF histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_generation_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance)) > 0.8
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = "page" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary = "Inference runtime p95 > 800ms", runbook = "/confluence/eng-platform/inference-runtime-runbook" }

- Contacts:
  - Primary oncall: see PagerDuty schedule.
  - Platform leads: Elena Rodriguez (platform-eng), Mateo Alvarez (obs), Priya Nair (serving-runtime).

10) Maintenance & ownership checklist (quarterly):

- Verify SLOs and budgets, adjust alert thresholds if false positives > 5% in last quarter.
- Run synthetic workload tests for top 10 models and compare to baseline.
- Audit dashboards: remove panels with no viewers in last 90 days.

--

If you are the owner of a service mentioned in this doc and your runbook or dashboard links are stale, update this page and add yourself to reviewers. For any immediate changes to alerts or runbooks, follow the change-management template in policies-and-process and notify the platform Slack channel.
